title: Joint KV-Cache Compression and Eviction
one_line_claim: EVICPRESS jointly optimizes KV-cache compression and eviction decisions per-context using a utility function balancing quality and latency trade-offs.
method_summary: EVICPRESS profiles all feasible eviction-compression configurations per context, scoring each via a unified utility function that quantifies quality-delay trade-offs. An offline phase pre-computes utility scores; an online phase selects configurations and applies periodic re-profiling when quality diverges from predictions.

key_findings.finding: Different contexts have different compression sensitivities; no single compression strategy is universally optimal.
key_findings.quote: Different contexts have different sensitivities to lossy compression errors; thus, simply applying the same eviction or compression schemes on all contexts is not optimal.

key_findings.finding: EVICPRESS reduces TTFT by 1.43-3.77x at the same generation quality and improves quality scores by 13.58-55.40% at the same TTFT.
key_findings.quote: EvicPress reduces TTFT by 1.43 to 3.77x at the same quality score, and improves quality scores by 13.58% to 55.40% at the same TTFT

key_findings.finding: Joint optimization of compression and eviction is necessary; treating them as independent leaves performance on the table.
key_findings.quote: Prior work misses an important aspect: jointly optimizing the eviction and compression decisions across all KV caches to minimize average generation latency without hurting quality.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV-cache compression effects on generation quality and model per-context sensitivity to compression.
differs_on: EVICPRESS jointly optimizes compression+eviction configurations via utility profiling before inference; HERALD predicts catastrophic failures from per-token logit signals during generation.
EVICPRESS evaluates configurations as a black box; HERALD explicitly models token-level logit distributions to forecast failure.
EVICPRESS provides online re-profiling and reconfiguration per context; HERALD operates via a frozen XGBoost model without online adaptation.
